title: Anchors taken from a 'likely' record (schools, people, handles, domains, company legal-name aliases) still confirm other records
evidence: Temp test through stepDeepCheck: Google given; record 1 (likely) yields school Stanford, origin weak:<id>; namesake 'charged with fraud' record graded confirmed, reasons 'names Google','names Stanford University'. Separately, alias {Zeta Holdings Inc, origin weak:x1} confirmed 'Jane Roe, director of Zeta Holdings Inc, was charged'.
scenario: Given company is a large employer (Google) or the name is a mononym. A likely record adds a Stanford school anchor (weak:). A namesake's fraud charge naming Google and Stanford is upgraded to confirmed by regrade() and becomes a red flag. A legal name learned by companyFacts from a likely record (weak:) also confirms any record naming it. This breaks the written rule that a likely record never confirms other records.
fix: In anchorNeeds, set a flag whenever any anchor in schools/people/handles/domains/aliases has a non-strong origin, not only companies. In gradeOf, when the grade is confirmed and that flag is set, grade again with viewOf keeping only strong-origin anchors of every kind (filter aliases by origin too). Cap at likely unless that strict grade still confirms. Add the two cases above as tests.
verifyNote: Reproduced via stepDeepCheck: 'Jane Roe of Google' graded likely added school Stanford (origin weak:id); a namesake 'charged with fraud' record naming Google and Stanford was graded confirmed. anchorNeeds flags only weak companies; matchSubject counts any school/person/handle/domain as the second fact. Breaks FOUNDER-CHECK rule 1.
betterFix: In anchorNeeds, flag any non-strong anchor of every kind, aliases included. On a confirmed grade, regrade with viewOf keeping only strong anchors. orgMatcher reads aliases from the original subject through a closure, so viewOf alone cannot hide weak aliases: pass the filtered alias map through (subject.anchors in the view) or give matchSubject a strongOnly option. Add both regression tests.

title: A shorter form of a multi-word company, or a legal form after it, lets 'Acme Robotics CEO Jane Doe met <subject>' confirm
scenario: Subject 'Eric Glyman' at 'Zeta Labs' (or 'Acme Robotics', 'Nikola Corporation'). Text: 'Zeta Labs CEO Jane Doe met Eric Glyman'. Result: confirmed. With 'Theranos' or 'Stripe' the same sentence is graded possible. companyMention gives two spans, 'Zeta Labs' [0,9] and 'Zeta' [0,4]. For the 'Zeta' span, OTHER_AFTER_COMPANY reads ' Labs CEO Jane…', which fails, so that pair is accepted. 'Nikola Corporation CEO Jane Doe' fails the same way because the legal form sits between the name and the role.
fix: In companyMentionMatcher, drop any span nested inside a longer span. In nameNearCompany, skip trailing legal forms, DESCRIPTORS and a ticker before testing OTHER_AFTER_COMPANY. Add a test for each multi-word company shape.
evidence: Temp jest: matchSubject(createSubject({name:'Eric Glyman',company:'Zeta Labs'}),'Zeta Labs CEO Jane Doe met Eric Glyman') gave confirmed. The same happened for Acme Robotics and Nikola Corporation; Theranos gave possible.
verifyNote: Reproduced: 'Zeta Labs/Acme Robotics/Nikola Corporation CEO Jane Doe met Eric Glyman' confirmed. Also 'Theranos Inc CEO Jane Doe met Eric Glyman' confirmed: a legal form after a one-word name defeats OTHER_AFTER_COMPANY too. Bare Theranos/Stripe gives possible.
betterFix: In nameNearCompany (companyFirst branch) test OTHER_AFTER_COMPANY against the text after the end of the longest company span that starts at or contains co, and skip an optional legal form, descriptor words and a (TICKER) first. Also drop spans nested inside a longer span in companyMentionMatcher. Add tests for each shape, including 'Theranos Inc CEO'.

title: '<Name>, CEO of Omega Corp, said <Company>…' confirms: the affiliation rule only reads lowercase role words
scenario: Subject 'Eric Glyman' at 'Theranos'. Text: 'Eric Glyman, CEO of Omega Corp, said Theranos is a competitor' gives confirmed, and so does 'Eric Glyman, the CEO of Omega Corp, …'. 'chief executive of Omega Corp' correctly gives possible. AFFILIATION_AFTER_NAME allows only [\p{Ll}-]+ words before of/at/from, so CEO, CFO, VP, COO, Co-Founder and Partner never mark the person as belonging to another firm.
fix: Allow any-case role words in that slot, for example (?:[\p{L}&-]+\s+){0,3}? limited to ROLE_WORDS, ROLE_TEXT or lowercase words. Add tests for CEO, Co-Founder and VP of Sales.
evidence: Temp jest: matchSubject with Theranos and the text above gave confirmed for 'CEO of' and 'the CEO of', and possible for 'chief executive of'.
verifyNote: Reproduced: 'Eric Glyman, CEO of Omega Corp, said Theranos…' and 'the CEO of' both confirmed; 'chief executive of' gives possible. AFFILIATION_AFTER_NAME only accepts [\p{Ll}-]+ words before of/at/from.
betterFix: Allow role tokens in any case in that slot: (?:(?:[\p{Ll}-]+|CEO|CTO|CFO|COO|CPO|VP|SVP|EVP|[Cc]o-?[Ff]ounder|[Ff]ounder|[Pp]artner|[Pp]resident|[Dd]irector|[Hh]ead)\s+){0,3}?. The existing 'ours' check keeps 'Eric Glyman, CEO of Ramp' confirmed; add tests for both.

title: Speaker lists, panels and pipe rows give the subject a company that belongs to the person listed before them
scenario: Subject 'Eric Glyman' at 'Theranos'. Each of these gives confirmed: 'Speakers: Jane Doe, Theranos, and Eric Glyman, Omega Corp'; 'Panel: Jane Doe (Theranos), Eric Glyman (Omega Corp)'; 'Jane Doe | Theranos | Eric Glyman | Omega Corp'. When the company comes first, nameNearCompany never checks whether another person's name sits right before it ('Jane Doe, X' or 'Jane Doe (X)'). isWholeField treats any pipe row in which the name fills a field as being about the subject, whatever the other fields say.
fix: When the company comes first, reject the pair if a capitalised two-word name ends right before the company followed by ', ' or ' (' and is not the subject. Extend AFFILIATION_AFTER_NAME to ', <Org>' and ' (<Org>)'. In isWholeField, require the company field to be adjacent to the name field with no other person-like field between them.
evidence: Temp jest gave confirmed for all three texts with Theranos and with Zeta Labs.
verifyNote: Reproduced all three: comma list, parenthesised panel, and pipe row each give confirmed for Theranos belonging to Jane Doe.
betterFix: Company-first: reject when a capitalised two-word non-subject name ends directly before the company separated by ', ' or ' ('. Name-first: treat ', <CapOrg>' / ' (<CapOrg>)' right after the name as affiliation. isWholeField: only pair the company field with the nearest person field (the company field should follow the subject's field with no other person-like field between).

title: Names with a lowercase particle (van, von der, de la, bin) never match as written: every record grades 'none'
scenario: For 'Daan van der Berg' at 'Zeta Labs', the text 'Daan van der Berg, founder of Zeta Labs, was charged' grades none. 'Ursula von der Leyen', 'Carlos de la Cruz' and 'Mohammed bin Salman' behave the same in their usual lowercase form. Typing 'Vincent Van Dijk' does not help against 'Vincent van Dijk'. Only Title Case or all-caps text matches. Line 425 requires every surname word to be capitalised. middleState rejects a lowercase particle typed with a capital. The quick brief and the deep check would both return an empty or clean-looking profile.
fix: In the capitalisation check, exempt words in SURNAME_PARTICLES and NAME_JOINERS that belong to the typed surname. In parsePersonName, attach particles to the surname whatever their case, and match them case-insensitively. Add tests for van, von der, de la, bin and al-.
evidence: Temp jest: personNameMatcher('Ludwig van Beethoven').kind('Ludwig van Beethoven said') returned 'none'. matchSubject for Daan van der Berg returned none.
verifyNote: Reproduced: personNameMatcher kind is 'none' for 'Ludwig van Beethoven', 'Carlos de la Cruz', 'Mohammed bin Salman' as written, and for typed 'Vincent Van Dijk' vs 'van Dijk'; matchSubject for Daan van der Berg returns none. Line 425 requires every name word capitalised.
betterFix: In the capitalised check exempt words in SURNAME_PARTICLES/NAME_JOINERS that are part of the parsed surname (or given), and compare particles case-insensitively; keep the requirement that the main surname word is capitalised so 'grace hopper' prose stays rejected. Add tests for van, von der, de la, bin, al-.

title: 'Patrick and John Collison founded Stripe' grades 'none' for Patrick: shared-surname lists drop true records
scenario: Subject 'Patrick Collison' at 'Stripe'. 'Patrick and John Collison founded Stripe in 2010' and 'Stripe, founded by brothers Patrick and John Collison' both give level none with weak 'other-given', so the record is dropped entirely and is not even possible. 'WeWork co-founders Adam and Rebekah Neumann' does the same for Adam Neumann. This is the standard press form for co-founding siblings and couples, which leaves the profile thin.
fix: Detect '<Given>(, <G2>)* (and|&) <G3> <Surname>' where the subject's given name is in the list. Report it as its own weak kind and grade it possible, or likely with the company beside it, never confirmed. Keep it out of 'other-given'.
evidence: Temp jest: matchSubject(Patrick Collison/Stripe) on both texts returned {level:'none', weak:'other-given'}.
verifyNote: Reproduced: 'Patrick and John Collison founded Stripe' and 'founded by brothers Patrick and John Collison' give none/other-given, so the record is dropped.
betterFix: Before the otherGiven weak scan, recognise '<SubjectGiven>(, <G>)* (and|&) <G> <Surname>' and emit a distinct weak kind ('shared-surname'); grade possible, or likely with the company in the same clause, never confirmed. Keep it out of other-given.

title: 'the Ramp founder' and 'Ramp co-CEO' are not read as the company, so true Ramp records fall to possible
scenario: Subject 'Eric Glyman' at 'Ramp' (saved run r9). 'Eric Glyman: How the Ramp Founder Is Reinventing Business Finance', 'Eric Glyman, the Ramp co-founder, said' and 'Ramp co-CEO Eric Glyman: spend $100…' all regrade to possible. A determiner before an ordinary word discards the mention before markerFor runs, even when a role word follows. 'co-ceo' is not in ROLE_WORDS.
fix: Skip the DETERMINERS rejection when the next word, or the word after a possessive, is a role word. Add co-ceo, co-chief, cofounder and co-founder variants to ROLE_WORDS.
evidence: Regraded r9 eric-glyman-ramp records with matchSubject: these records went from confirmed to possible. Isolated temp tests confirmed each of the three texts.
verifyNote: Reproduced: all three Ramp texts grade possible. Line 828 drops an ordinary-word company after a determiner before markerFor runs.
betterFix: Skip the DETERMINERS rejection when the next word (or after 's) is a ROLE_WORDS/BUSINESS_WORDS entry; add co-ceo, co-chief and cofounder variants to ROLE_WORDS (and to OTHER_AFTER_COMPANY so 'Ramp co-CEO Jane Doe' still blocks another person).

title: A ticker in brackets after the company ('Nikola (NKLA) founder') is read as part of a longer name
scenario: Subject 'Trevor Milton' at 'Nikola'. The saved r9 record 'Nikola (NKLA) founder Trevor Milton indicted on three counts of fraud' regrades from confirmed to possible. insideLongerName treats '(NKLA)' as a capitalised next word that continues another name, so the mention is dropped.
fix: In insideLongerName, ignore a following parenthesised ticker or exchange tag, such as (ABCD) or (NASDAQ: ABCD), and look at the word after it.
evidence: Temp jest: matchSubject(Trevor Milton/Nikola, the text above) returned possible.
verifyNote: Reproduced: 'Nikola (NKLA) founder Trevor Milton…' grades possible; startsCapital('(NKLA)') is true so insideLongerName rejects.
betterFix: In insideLongerName treat a following parenthesised all-caps ticker or '(NASDAQ: X)' tag as neutral and read the word after it for role/verb; same skip in markerFor's next-word lookup.

title: 'Ex-Nikola CEO Trevor Milton' does not name Nikola: the hyphen guard also blocks 'ex-'
scenario: Subject 'Trevor Milton' at 'Nikola'. The saved r9 record 'Ex-Nikola CEO Trevor Milton ready for takeoff with SyberJet' regrades to possible, while 'Former Nikola CEO …' gives confirmed. The (?<!\p{L}-) lookbehind meant to block 'on-ramp' also blocks 'ex-Nikola', 'ex-Google' and 'ex-Stripe'.
fix: Allow the match when the hyphenated prefix is 'ex' (case-insensitive), for example by adding (?<!(?<![\p{L}])(?!ex-)\p{L}+-) or a post-check that the prefix word is 'ex'.
evidence: Temp jest: matchSubject gave possible for 'Ex-Nikola' and confirmed for 'Former Nikola'.
verifyNote: Reproduced: 'Ex-Nikola CEO Trevor Milton' and 'ex-Stripe engineer John Smith' give possible; 'Former Nikola CEO' confirmed. The (?<!\p{L}-) lookbehind blocks ex-.
betterFix: Replace the lookbehind with a post-check: if the char before is '-', allow the match only when the preceding hyphenated word is 'ex' (case-insensitive) or 'non'? no, only 'ex'; keep blocking 'on-ramp'. Apply the same in OTHER_BEFORE/after contexts.

title: Registered names with a describing word (Coinbase Global, Robinhood Markets, FTX Trading, Nikola Motor) never match the press
scenario: Typed company 'Coinbase Global, Inc.': 'Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong was sued' gives possible. The same happens for 'Robinhood Markets, Inc.', 'FTX Trading Ltd.', 'Nikola Motor Company', 'Rivian Automotive', 'Moderna Therapeutics' and 'Ramp Business Corporation'. COMPANY_GENERIC, which builds the short key, lacks global, markets, trading, motor, business, automotive, therapeutics and similar words, although DESCRIPTORS has most of them. The only match form stays two words, and the audit fix for critic-foreign-legal-forms covered legal forms only.
fix: Build the loose key by also removing DESCRIPTORS plus business, automotive and similar words, when what remains is one distinctive word (not RESIDUE_STOP, not ordinary). Keep ordinary words behind the existing marker rules.
evidence: Temp jest: companyMatchForms('Coinbase Global, Inc.') gave a single form 'coinbase global', and companyMention returned none. matchSubject returned possible.
verifyNote: Reproduced: companyMatchForms('Coinbase Global, Inc.') yields only 'coinbase global'; Coinbase, Robinhood Markets, Nikola Motor Company typed names give possible for plain press text.
betterFix: Also derive a loose form by stripping DESCRIPTORS plus business/automotive/therapeutics/markets/global/trading/motor when one distinctive word remains (not RESIDUE_STOP, not ORDINARY, not a place); ordinary-word results keep marker rules.

title: Common written forms of the full name grade 'none': a quoted nickname inside the name, and a double surname with or without a hyphen
scenario: Subject 'William McFarland' at 'Fyre Media'. The text 'William "Billy" McFarland, founder of Fyre Media, was sentenced' gives none, the usual form in DOJ and press records. 'Maria Garcia-Lopez' against 'Maria Garcia Lopez' gives none both ways, not even a weak kind. 'Sam Bankman-Fried' against 'Sam Bankman Fried' gives none. MIDDLE cannot hold a quoted token, and a surname's hyphen and space are not interchangeable.
fix: Let MIDDLE accept a quoted nickname (["“'‘]\p{L}+["”'’]) and treat it as an acceptable middle. In surnameRe, join surname parts with (?:-|\s+). When the typed surname has a hyphen, also accept the space form.
evidence: Temp jest: personNameMatcher('William McFarland').kind(...) returned 'none'. Maria Garcia-Lopez and Maria Garcia Lopez returned 'none' in both directions.
verifyNote: Reproduced: William "Billy" McFarland gives none (also via matchSubject); Garcia-Lopez vs Garcia Lopez and Bankman Fried vs Bankman-Fried give none in both directions.
betterFix: Let MIDDLE accept one quoted token and treat it as an acceptable middle (not other-middle). In surnameRe join multi-part surnames with (?:-|\s+), and split a typed hyphenated surname so the space form matches; keep the longer-surname guard for extra parts.

title: 'born <Place>' after the name becomes another name of the person ('Kansas City'), which then ties unrelated records
scenario: A confirmed record reads 'Jane Doe (born Kansas City, Missouri) is the founder of Zeta Labs'. findNameAliases returns 'Kansas City' (how: born), and deepCheck.readNameAliases passes it to addNameAlias, which accepts it because it parses with a surname. After that, 'Kansas City police said a Zeta Labs truck crashed' grades likely, 'Kansas City' alone grades possible, and the report lists 'Kansas City' as one of the person's names. 'born South Korea' gives 'South Korea' the same way. 'also known as JD Capital Partners' gives a company as a name.
fix: For the 'born' cue, require the alias to share a token with the subject's name, or to be followed by ';' or ')' plus a year. Reject candidates that end in an organisation word, a legal form or COMPANY_GENERIC. In addNameAlias, refuse names whose surname part is a RESIDUE_STOP or place word.
evidence: Temp jest: findNameAliases returned Kansas City, South Korea and JD Capital Partners. After addNameAlias('Kansas City'), matchSubject gave likely with basis company and alias.
verifyNote: Reproduced: findNameAliases returns 'Kansas City' and 'South Korea' (born) and 'JD Capital Partners' (aka); addNameAlias accepts 'Kansas City'; then 'Kansas City police said a Zeta Labs truck crashed' grades likely.
betterFix: For 'born', reject when followed by ', <Place>' or ' in', or when the name ends a place/country/state word; require a token shared with the subject's given name or a clearly personal shape. For all cues reject names ending in LEGAL_FORMS/COMPANY_GENERIC/org words. Have addNameAlias refuse surnames that are RESIDUE_STOP, place or org words.

title: Unlisted titles before the name (Admiral, Pastor, Sheikh, Prince, a company used as a modifier) make a true mention 'other-given' and drop it
scenario: 'the late Admiral Elizabeth Holmes', 'a lawsuit against Theranos Elizabeth Holmes', 'with Ramp Eric Glyman' and 'the pioneering Navy Grace Hopper' all give other-given, so matchSubject returns none. Any capitalised word after a lowercase word that is missing from NOT_A_GIVEN or TITLES counts as another given name. In COMMON_GIVEN, words such as Mark, Young, Christian, Grace, Frank and Long trigger it even in headlines ('Investors Mark Elizabeth Holmes Release').
fix: Add admiral, commander, pastor, rabbi, bishop, imam, sheikh, prince, princess, king, queen, emir, baron, laureate, billionaire, entrepreneur and co-ceo to NOT_A_GIVEN. Skip the rule when the previous word is a known company anchor or ends a company match. Grade 'other-given' as possible rather than none when the subject's company sits beside it.
evidence: Temp jest: personNameMatcher('Elizabeth Holmes').kind on each text returned 'other-given'.
verifyNote: Reproduced: all four texts give other-given and matchSubject none, even with Theranos named. Mostly rare wordings, so low is right.
betterFix: Add admiral, commander, pastor, rabbi, bishop, imam, sheikh, prince, princess, king, queen, emir, baron, billionaire, entrepreneur to NOT_A_GIVEN; skip the rule when the previous word ends a company span; in a Title Case headline only count COMMON_GIVEN words that are not also ordinary verbs (mark, grace, frank, young).
